newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-WestLB posts steep H1 earnings rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-WestLB posts steep H1 earnings rise.

text.p: Westdeutsche Landesbank (WestLB), Germany's largest publicly-owned bank, on Thursday reported a 35 percent rise in first-half operating profit as rallying financial markets boosted trading profits.

The bank, regarded as a potential predator in Europe's rapidly consolidating bank sector, said operating profit after provisions for bad debt rose to 749.6 million marks. That compares with 611.5 million in the first six months of 1996.
"Our intensified investment banking and treasury activities are increasingly proving to be an important source of earnings for the bank," chief executive Friedel Neuber said in a statement.
Heavy investment in these activities was paying off, boosting net interest and trading income, while costs were stable, Neuber said.
"We expect the positive earnings trend to be maintained throughout the whole of 1997."
The earnings growth follows a trend towards steep profit gains at Germany's big banks as the recent stock market rally has boosted trading and commission income.
Net interest income rose to 1.93 billion marks, up 4.8 percent from 1.84 billion in the year-earlier period.
Own-account trading income climbed 49 percent to 274.0 million marks while net commission income rose 6.7 percent to 374.3 million.

WestLB matches the country's traditional banking giants not only in size but also in global ambition. Neuber said recently his bank was in talks with European banks with a view to acquiring a stake, but did not specify possible contenders.

Under Neuber's leadership, WestLB has gained an aggressive reputation, grabbing a share of the tourism market via stakes in tour operator TUI, charter airline LTU and British travel agent Thomas Cook.

It bought Panmure Gordon, a British stockbroker, and Quorum Capital Management Ltd, a British asset manager, last year and has been expanding its London-based investment banking arm West Merchant Bank Ltd.
The group balance sheet total rose to 520.4 billion marks by June 30 from 465.8 billion marks at the end of December.
